title: ID0423446-DC/Si-D/AE-[MP / R5 170001908] Low power issue
description:
Reported behaviour/issue: Outlet 1 is delivering significantly lower power compared to Outlet 2.
Solution:
05/15/2025: Charger configuration changed to older configuration in order to get the outlets available for charging but with low power due to power converter issue.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0423446-DC/Si-D/AE-[MP / R5 170001908] Low power issue CRM:02698000114
additional_info.body:
Hi Nadeem,
I hope this email finds you well.
EV functions as the Master & charger functions as Slave. The charger provides the current and voltage that the EV demanded.
The EV’s target current changed, and the EVSE current adjusted accordingly. EV charging operates on the principles of Constant Current (CC) and Constant Voltage (CV). Initially, the EV charges up to 80% SOC using CC, and then it switches to CV mode gradually based on EV requirements. During this phase, the EV's target current drops to protect the battery from thermal runaway and to ensure proper cell balancing.
Apart from it, it would be great if you could provide the timestamp or the date so that we can analyse it and share the root cause of the same.
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Shrey

additional_info.subject: Re: ID0423446-DC/Si-D/AE-[MP / R5 170001908] Low power issue CRM:02698000114
additional_info.body:
Dear Shrey,
Thank you for your previous response regarding the functioning of the EV charger.
However, the reply did not fully address our concern. Kindly note that the charger in question is a 160kW model with both outlets configured as CCS2. Originally, the charger was equipped with CHAdeMO and CCS2, which is evident from the serial number.
Following the recent cable retrofit work carried out by Siemens, we have observed that the HMI display now shows an output of 60kW for Outlet 1 and 100kW for Outlet 2. This is not in line with the expected configuration for a 160kW charger.
We had expected that the power module configuration details could be confirmed via the SCB.
We kindly request you to review the current configuration and take the necessary steps to ensure both outlets are correctly configured and capable of utilizing the full capacity of the charger.
Your prompt attention to this matter will be appreciated.
Regards,
Nadeem

Dear Colleagues,
I am writing to formally inform that we are moving case 0423446 ﻿from the
eMobility DC Queue (Level 2)
to the
eMobility RC-AE SI E Queue (Level 2)
, due to one or more following reason (s):
Reason
Applicable
Onsite Repair (Component Exchange)
Maybe
Onsite Troubleshooting
Yes
End Customer Communication
Yes
Spare Part Ordering
Maybe
Performance monitoring by RC
Could you please follow the below troubleshooting steps as mentioned below.
1
. Please check if the power converter are properly connection to its shelf case.
2
. Check for any loose connection of any power cable or CAN communication cables of the converter and measured the voltage across it with the help of multimeter. Check the resistance across CAN communication cables.
3
. Please see to the display of the power converter whether it is OFF state or ON?
4
. Try swapping the power converter with the good one and if the error flag was changed to the replaced one then we can suspect that the converter is faulty.
5
. If all the steps are performed and you still see the power converter are faulty, we suggest you to replace it as we can't rework to it. Apart from it, please check the power housing of the power converter, there might be chances that the wiring is defective.
MLFB :  8EM5903-0AA01-0AA2 (Power Converter AC/DC 20kW)

https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=zTuuOHmV1E-t2rQuFJXVWmj9a-TsNwNBlbUVnW64LEtUNU5QSU5XUjA2VkpPUTJJTzJENDhaSTZMMi4u
